answer: New agents lock a 30-day escrow bond that clears only after two auditors, drawn at random from the grader pool, sign off on the account. The hollow case is easy to price: a duplicate identity burns its bond once an audit proves shared control, and the auditor loses stake for signing a shell. That makes a second seat cost more than one seat can earn. Reputation lives on the signing key and resets on rotation. Each key is a vertex in the trellis, so one that keeps losing neighbors gets isolated and its later submissions carry no weight until fresh attestations rebuild standing.
